exam: 2008 AP Chemistry MCQ · Version indicated in source
text:
Questions 10-11 refer to the following.

     (A)   Activation energy
      (B)  Enthalpy of formation
      (C)  Entropy
     (D)  Gibbs free energy
      (E)   Lattice energy

11.  Quantity typically determined by measuring the
           rate of a reaction at two or more different
         temperatures





2

stimulus.verificationNote: Page 31 explicitly labels Questions 10–11; includes the shared term list A-E.

crop.note: Compared complete individual crop for Question 11 against original 2008 source page. Common context is linked via stimulus-2008-mcq-10-11-page31; individual stem and choices are separate and complete.

candidates.name: Collision model and temperature effects
candidates.definition: Explaining rate changes through collision frequency, the fraction of collisions with energy at least Ea (Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution), and correct orientation.
candidates.include: Tag when a change in rate with temperature, concentration or orientation must be explained at the particle level.
candidates.exclude: Numerical Arrhenius-equation calculations are not assessed.

candidates.name: Entropy
candidates.definition: Predicting and explaining the sign of ΔS from dispersal of matter and energy (phase, moles of gas, volume, temperature), and calculating ΔS° from standard molar entropies.
candidates.include: Tag when the sign or value of an entropy change must be predicted, explained or calculated, or substances ranked by entropy.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ΔG sign analysis unless the entropy sign must be determined as part of it (then entropy is supporting).

candidates.name: Gibbs free energy and favorability
candidates.definition: Using ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS° and the signs of ΔH and ΔS to determine thermodynamic favorability and the temperature at which favorability changes.
candidates.include: Tag when ΔG must be calculated or its sign reasoned from ΔH and ΔS, or a crossover temperature found.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ΔG-K or ΔG-E relationships alone (tag free-energy-equilibrium or cell-potential).

candidates.name: Ionic solids and lattice attraction
candidates.definition: The structure of ionic solids as lattices of alternating cations and anions, and comparing the strength of lattice attraction from ion charge and ion size.
candidates.include: Tag when ionic compounds are compared by melting point, lattice energy or hardness using ion charge and radius, or the lattice structure is described.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag classification of a solid as ionic without a lattice-strength argument (tag solid-types).

candidates.name: Kinetic molecular theory
candidates.definition: Explaining gas behavior from particle motion: average kinetic energy proportional to absolute temperature, speed depending on molar mass, Maxwell-Boltzmann distributions, and pressure from collisions.
candidates.include: Tag when particle speed, kinetic energy, collision frequency or a speed distribution must be compared or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag numerical ideal-gas calculations with no particle-level reasoning; numerical Graham's-law calculations are not assessed.

candidates.name: Activation energy and energy profiles
candidates.definition: Reading single- and multi-step reaction energy profiles: activation energy, transition states, intermediates, forward and reverse barriers, the rate-limiting barrier, and overall ΔH.
candidates.include: Tag when an energy profile must be read, drawn or used, or activation energies compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag simple enthalpy diagrams with no activation barrier (tag endo-exothermic).

candidates.name: Catalysis
candidates.definition: How catalysts increase rate by providing an alternative mechanism with lower activation energy while being regenerated and leaving ΔH and K unchanged.
candidates.include: Tag when a catalyst's effect on mechanism, energy profile, rate, ΔH or equilibrium must be identified or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag intermediates questions without a catalyst.
